name: HSWM Cellular Runtime Kernel
purpose: Authorize, replay, and expose adapter effects for typed HSWM cell activations without allowing model calls or external mutation inside the reducer.

current_consumers: hswm_cellular_store.py SQLite event store and transactional outbox
hswm_cellular_openai.py OpenAI-compatible and deterministic fixture ports
fit_evidence: The boundary owns shared activation state, version checks, budgets, replay, and typed rejection semantics.
Formal and executable consumers require the same command-event-effect vocabulary.
Multiple model and persistence adapters can share the kernel without importing prompt or storage policy.
alternatives_considered: A helper module was rejected because activation ordering, replay, and budget ownership are shared protocol concerns.
A model wrapper was rejected because model invocation is an external effect rather than kernel authority.
A full scheduler was deferred because scheduling and topology policy are explicit non-goals of slice 1.

boundary.owns: Typed activation admission, optimistic version checks, budget consumption, pending/completed correlation, deterministic replay, and effect description.
boundary.mechanism: Pure decide(state, command), evolve(state, event), effects(event), and replay(initial, history) functions over versioned commands and events.
boundary.state_authority: The committed SQLite event sequence is authoritative. Each accepted command atomically commits events, stream state, command receipt, and effect intents under one BEGIN IMMEDIATE boundary; the pure reducer remains storage-independent.
policy_outside: Which cell to select or schedule
Semantic weight update or credit assignment
non_goals: Proving that connected cells constitute a larger AI

state_model.version: Monotone event sequence used for optimistic conflict rejection.
state_model.remaining_budget: Natural-number authority consumed exactly once by each accepted request event.
state_model.pending: Activation-correlated cell, input digest, and expected output type.
state_model.completed: Activation-correlated output identity and digest; raw adapter state is excluded.

protocol.versioning: All v1 Python records use hswm-cellular-runtime/v1; breaking field or semantic changes require a new protocol version and replay migration.

invariants: Rejected commands emit no events, consume no budget, and expose no effects.
Every accepted event sequence equals the prior state version plus one.
An accepted request consumes exactly one budget unit and creates exactly one pending activation.
An activation identifier cannot be pending or completed twice.
Completion requires a pending activation and its declared output packet type.
Completion preserves remaining budget and removes the matching pending activation.
Only CellStepRequested exposes InvokeCell; CellStepCompleted exposes no effect.
Replay of the same initial state and ordered history yields the same state digest.
ports: CellPort.invoke executes one InvokeCell effect and returns a typed PacketEnvelope.
SqliteCellRuntime atomically appends accepted events under expected version and owns the transactional outbox.
Future SnapshotStore accelerates replay without becoming authoritative.

runtime.ordering: Per kernel state, events are totally ordered by contiguous natural-number sequence.
runtime.concurrency: Commands use optimistic expected_version checks; SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes competing writers and outbox claims per database.
runtime.backpressure: remaining_budget rejects new requests at zero; queue capacity and fair scheduling are outside this slice.
runtime.cancellation: Not present in v1; cancellation requires a versioned command/event pair before implementation.
runtime.timeouts: The pure kernel has no clock; adapter hosts own timeouts and must record any resulting terminal event in a later protocol version.

durability.persistence: SQLite WAL with synchronous FULL persists streams, events, command receipts, and outbox records; committed state is integrity-checked against deterministic replay.
durability.atomic_commit: BEGIN IMMEDIATE atomically commits request events and pending outbox effects, and atomically commits completion events with terminal outbox success.
durability.recovery: Reopening the database recovers pending effects and deterministic stream state. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME effects remain suspended until explicit reconciliation or abandonment.
durability.effect_idempotency: activation_id and intent SHA-256 provide exact-retry receipts and conflicting-intent rejection. X-Idempotency-Key is sent to the model endpoint, but exactly-once external execution is not claimed.
durability.migration: SQLite user_version 1 and protocol v1 are immutable. Forward schema migration and event upcasters remain production promotion gates.

failure_model: Stale versions, exhausted budget, duplicate activation, unknown cell, type mismatch, and unknown completion are typed rejections.
An invalid event that bypasses admission raises KernelInvariantError during Python replay.
Adapter failure occurs outside the reducer and cannot manufacture a completion event.
Crash-after-commit-before-effect recovers a pending outbox record; ambiguous after-send failures become UNKNOWN_OUTCOME and are never automatically retried.
Durable approval state, stale in-flight lease recovery, and endpoint-side idempotency receipts remain production promotion gates.

traces: activation_id correlation across request event, invoke effect, and completion event
event sequence and cell_id for each committed transition
metrics: accepted and rejected command counts by rejection reason
pending activation count and remaining budget
adapter latency outside the pure kernel
observability.redaction: Receipts and state projections retain packet identifiers and SHA-256 digests but exclude packet payloads and model-private adapter state.

security: Packet payload and provenance must be canonical JSON before digesting.
Cell contracts are injected as trusted deterministic configuration for slice 1.
Reducers perform no filesystem, network, environment, random, clock, or subprocess access.
External adapters must enforce secret isolation and output-size limits before returning a packet.
verification: Lean compilation with no sorry or admit for the command-event-effect invariants.
Python tests for the happy path, every v1 rejection family, deterministic replay, effect separation, and adapter injection.
Longinus hash and symbol binding verification across Lean, Python, tests, specification, and receipt.
implementation_slices: Slice 1 complete: pure Lean and Python runtime kernel plus one injected CellPort vertical path.
Slice 2 engineering gate complete: atomic SQLite EventStore and transactional outbox with named crash-window tests; durable approvals and lease-expiry recovery remain promotion work.
Slice 3 bounded smoke complete: deterministic fixture plus one actual qwen3.6-27b OpenAI-compatible activation; endpoint-side idempotency receipt remains promotion work.
Slice 4: typed semantic-synapse planner that submits commands without gaining state authority.
falsifiers: Collapse the engine to a helper module if versioned shared state, replay, and multiple adapters are removed.
Reject production promotion if a model call can occur before request-event commit.
Reject production promotion if crash replay can duplicate an external model invocation without an idempotency receipt.
Reject the Lean-Python correspondence claim if any named command, event, rejection, transition, or effect has divergent semantics.
